rationale: Registry entry 'case-study-lightbox' has allowed_action REUSE_WITH_VERIFICATION, catalog_status packaged-react-0.2.0-rc.0, and CaseStudyImageLightbox is a confirmed export in src/index.ts. The component API (images, activeIndex, onSelect, onClose) exactly covers the requirements: keyboard arrow navigation (ArrowLeft/ArrowRight in source keydown handler), Escape to close (Escape key handler), modal focus trap, and focus-return-to-opener on close (useEffect capturing opener before open and calling focus() on cleanup). Three public-domain placeholder images from picsum.photos are used — no unlicensed or private assets. The local npm tarball (krpadesigns-portfolio-design-system-0.2.0-rc.0.tgz) was installed directly into the consumer as authorized.

warnings: 'use client' directives in package dist files ignored by Vite bundler — expected; not an error

testing_limitations: No interactive browser test run — keyboard navigation (ArrowLeft, ArrowRight, Escape), focus-trap, focus-return, zoom controls, and reduced-motion behavior were not independently verified in a live browser.
Storybook story 06-interactive-storytelling-patterns--case-study-lightbox was not rendered during this evaluation.
picsum.photos URLs require a live network connection; placeholder images were not fetched or verified offline.
Mobile viewport overflow and responsive layout were not tested at 390px or 768px.
Screen-reader / ARIA dialog announcement not independently audited.
human_review_needed: Interactive browser keyboard test: Tab/Shift+Tab focus trap, ArrowLeft/ArrowRight gallery navigation, Escape close, focus-return-to-trigger.
Verify zoom controls do not overflow viewport on small screens.
Confirm picsum.photos images are acceptable as case-study placeholders in this context.
Accessibility audit: role=dialog, aria-modal, aria-label, reduced-motion preference.

Confirm CaseStudyImageLightbox opener focus-capture behavior works correctly when triggered from a button (useEffect captures document.activeElement at open time — verify timing is correct in React 19).
